'''John K. Hall''' (born 1940) is an American-born marine geophysicist, known for his work in [[marine geology]], [[Bathymetry|bathymetric]] [[Cartography|mapping]], and Arctic research. 

He is known for development of [[Digital elevation model|digital terrain models]] (DTMs) and [[Bathymetry|bathymetric]] surveys for various regions of the world.<ref>{{Cite web |title=First part of Dr. John K. Hall data (International Bathymetric Charts of the Mediterranean Sea and other documents) |url=https://emodnet.ec.europa.eu/geonetwork/srv/api/records/de4240bd-26c5-4bb2-a4de-9042d9ff5cc0 |website=Emodnet}}</ref> He has also led work in bathymetric charting of the [[Mediterranean Sea|Mediterranean]], [[Black Sea]], and [[North American Arctic|Arctic regions]], as well as in the National Bathymetric [[Survey of Israel]]. In 2020, he was awarded the Medallion of the [[Israel Geological Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=פרסים {{!}} Israel Geological Society |url=https://en.igs.org.il/awards |access-date=2025-01-06 |website=IsraelGeoSociety |language=en}}</ref>

== Early life==
Hall was born April 14, 1940 in [[Waltham, Massachusetts]]. <ref name=":0">{{Cite web |date=2024-06-11 |title=COA Discussion Group: Observations from Israel with Former Resident Dr. John K. Hall |url=https://westonowl.com/2024/06/11/coa-discussion-group-observations-from-israel-with-former-resident-dr-john-k-hall/ |access-date=2025-01-06 |website=Weston Owl |language=en-GB}}</ref> He earned a Bachelor of Science degree in Geology from [[Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute]] (RPI) in [[Troy, New York]], in 1962.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |title=John K. Hall |url=https://exeter.edu/people/john-k-hall/ |access-date=2025-01-06 |website=Phillips Exeter Academy |language=en-US}}</ref> He then completed his Ph.D. in Marine Geophysics at [[Columbia University]]’s [[Lamont–Doherty Earth Observatory|Lamont-Doherty Geological Observatory]] (LDGO) in 1970, where he conducted research on the [[Arctic Ocean]], including studies of the Alpha-Mendeleev Ridge.<ref name=":2">https://www.ldeo.columbia.edu/sites/default/files/uploaded/image/John%20Hall.pdf

Alumni Profile: John K. Hall, PhD ’70 After completing a doctorate in marine</ref>

== Career ==
Hall began his professional career as a marine geophysicist at the [[Woods Hole Oceanographic Institution]] (WHOI) before moving to Israel in 1970. <ref name=":0" />He became the first marine geophysicist at the Geological Survey of Israel (GSI), where he established the Israel National Bathymetric Survey. <ref>{{Cite web |date=2010-06-07 |title=John K Hall {{!}} Nautilus Live |url=https://nautiluslive.org/people/john-k-hall |access-date=2025-01-06 |website=nautiluslive.org |language=en}}</ref>

Throughout his career, He was involved in the compilation of bathymetric data for various international projects, including the International Bathymetric Chart of the Mediterranean (IBCM) and the [[General Bathymetric Chart of the Oceans]],<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-08-10 |title=The IBCAO 4.0 Bathymetric Chart: New Depth Map of the Arctic Ocean |url=https://scitechdaily.com/the-ibcao-4-0-bathymetric-chart-new-depth-map-of-the-arctic-ocean/ |access-date=2025-01-06 |website=SciTechDaily |language=en-US}}</ref> where he contributed to the Mediterranean Sea bathymetry. <ref>{{Cite web |title=Details of Second part of Dr. John K. Hall data (International Bathymetric Charts of the Mediterranean Sea, Relief Maps of Israel and Cyprus, etc.) |url=https://www.emodnet-ingestion.eu/submissions/submissions_details.php?menu=39&tpd=745&step=018Bathymetry_00832 |website=EmodNet}}</ref>

He also collaborate with [[University of Haifa]] and the [[University of New Hampshire]]'s Center for Coastal and Ocean Mapping (UNH-CCOM), to  furthered advancements in marine geophysics and geoinformatics. <ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Beaudoin |first1=Jonathan |last2=Sade |first2=Aharon |last3=Schulze |first3=Boris |last4=Hall |first4=John |date=2011-12-19 |title=Dead Sea Multi-beam Echo Sounder Survey |url=https://scholars.unh.edu/ccom/1064/ |journal=Hydro International |volume=15}}</ref>

He co-founded the Neev Center for Geoinformatics at the [[Hebrew University of Jerusalem]] (HUJI) in 2011.<ref name=":1" /> Hall also developed the first [[Digital elevation model|digital terrain model]] for Israel.<ref name=":2" />

===Hovercraft R/H Sabvabaa===

Hall is also the owner of the research hovercraft R/H Sabvabaa, which he funded and designed the construction of in 2007 with Yngve Kristoffersen of Norway’s [[University of Bergen|Bergen University]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Polar Hovercraft "Sabvabaa" {{!}} Main / Background browse |url=https://www.uib.no/geo/ |access-date=2025-01-06 |website=www.geo.uib.no}}</ref> In recent years, the hovercraft has been involved in [[Antarctic]] research, where it continues to support scientific exploration of remote ice-covered marine environments.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hall |first1=John K. |last2=Kristoffersen |first2=Yngve |date=2009-08-01 |title=The R/H Sabvabaa—A research hovercraft for marine geophysical work in the most inaccessible area of the Arctic Ocean |url=https://pubs.geoscienceworld.org/seg/tle/article-abstract/28/8/932/135798/The-R-H-Sabvabaa-A-research-hovercraft-for-marine?redirectedFrom=fulltext |journal=The Leading Edge |volume=28 |issue=8 |pages=932–935 |doi=10.1190/1.3192839 |bibcode=2009LeaEd..28..932H |issn=1070-485X|url-access=subscription }}</ref>

== Personal life ==
He is married to Israeli engineer anfd scientist Chava Fischler.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite journal |date=1968-11-07 |title=Electroacoustic amplifier has separate elements |url=https://www.worldradiohistory.com/Archive-Electronic-Design/1968/Electronic-Design-V16-N23-1968-1107.pdf |journal=Electronic Design |volume=16 |issue=23 |pages=22}}</ref> They moved to Israel in 1970 after Hall completed his Ph.D.<ref name=":2" /> Fischler received her M.Sc. in physics from Hebrew University, and a Ph.D. from the University of Delaware in 1966.<ref>{{Cite web |date=1966-06-12 |title=The 117th Commencement: Program of the Conferring of Degrees at the University of Delaware |url=https://archive.computerhistory.org/resources/access/text/2019/10/102783426-05-01-acc.pdf |access-date=2026-06-17 |website=Computer History Museum}}</ref>

Hall's grandfather was the head of the [[American Chicle Company]]. An inheritance allowed Hall to privately purchase a [[Multibeam echosounder|swath sonar device]] and a [[hovercraft]], both of which he has utilized in his research.<ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite news |last=Madrigal |first=Alexis |title=Hunting Arctic Asteroid Impact With Hovercraft |url=https://www.wired.com/2009/10/arctichovercraft/ |access-date=2026-06-17 |work=Wired |language=en-US |issn=1059-1028}}</ref>

==Awards==

Hall received the [[Israel Geological Society]] Raphael Freund Prize in 1999 and the Israel Cartographic Society Prize in 2004. <ref name=":1" />
